aclint.title: HP ACLINT
notes: The HP ACLINT is mapped at 0x02000000. The shared implementation provides two addressable hart slots, and hart slot 1 drives the HP software and timer interrupt inputs. MSIP1 is at offset 0x0004, MTIMECMP1 at 0x4008/0x400C, and the common MTIME at 0xBFF8/0xBFFC. This is separate from the management CLINT at 0x02010000.

Each 64-bit timer value is accessed as two 32-bit words. Use the retry and safe compare-update sequences below. The HP boot configuration uses a 1 MHz reference timebase; changing a CPU PLL setting does not redefine this reference.
software_steps: HP consumes hart slot 1 of the two-slot window. Do not use a management-CLINT base-address helper.
Read high/low/high and retry if the high words differ when a coherent RV32 time value is required.
Update compare using the safe high/low sequence. OpenSBI may provide this service for HP software.

plic.title: HP PLIC

apu.title: Audio Processing Unit
notes: The current capability word is 0x000001BD: WAV, FLAC, private DMA, ring, stream, sequencer and resampler bits are set. MP3 and KWS bits remain clear. Capability is not evidence that every production codec corpus or physical release gate is complete.

LP loads a bounded APUMC image before submitting work. Current RTL has 2048 64-bit control-store words (16 KiB), CAPABILITY1=0x01827010 and APB version 1.0. The 4096-word/32 KiB and V1.1 capacity refreeze is for subsequent implementation.
The loader checks header, ABI, bounds, entry descriptors and CRC before publishing valid/lock state. Rejected or aborted loads must leave stale instructions unexecutable.

Direct jobs use JOB_* staging registers; ring jobs use descriptor ownership and producer/consumer rules. Buffer limits, codec entry bounds, ownership, quiesce and transport completion participate in admission and termination.

The codec controller coordinates parser microcode, transport and processing primitives. Private DMA moves input/output while the stream router connects permitted audio paths. Capabilities do not waive rate, format, microcode or lifecycle checks.
On a fault, inspect retained stage/address/detail and consumed/produced counts, acknowledge the correct IRQ causes, and stop or reset the appropriate lifecycle level before reusing buffers.
software_steps: Probe information and capability through rs_apu_probe; reject codecs and formats not advertised by this snapshot.
Obtain ownership and configure allowed buffer ranges. Publish an aligned image and call rs_apu_microcode_load with a bounded timeout.
Check successful image validation before configuring a direct job or publishing ring descriptors. Set rate/channel/format expectations and valid input/output ranges.
Use the job/ring APIs declared in apu.h with the required fences and cache maintenance.
Wait for a terminal result and inspect counts, errors and IRQs. Successful transport alone does not establish full codec qualification.

mpw-timer.title: MPW User Timer
notes: The selected timer has an 8-bit divider and a live 16-bit counter. The divider cycles from zero through DIV, then emits an increment condition. COUNT increments on that condition, except that 0xFFFF clears to zero on the next user clock. A software COUNT write preloads the current count and takes precedence over normal updates; it is not an independently programmed auto-reload register.

At terminal count, a single output state toggles and is replicated on every selected user-GPIO output. The block continuously asserts its user output-enable vector. There is no run-enable bit or local output-mask register; root selection and pad ownership must be established before enabling the user path. Divider, count and output state reset to zero.

Both demo IPs complete APB access with PREADY=1 and PSLVERR=0. Only address bits 7:0 are decoded, so the local register pattern aliases every 256 bytes. Undefined reads return zero and undefined writes have no effect. These legacy blocks ignore PSTRB; software must use aligned full-word accesses. Neither block has a FIFO, DMA engine or dedicated interrupt.
software_steps: Run only with the committed MPW configuration and a board-safe user-GPIO ownership mask. The PRODUCT user-IP aperture does not instantiate this selectable demo.
Probe the expected slot and check its identifier before accessing local registers; the probe selects that slot through SYSCTRL. Check every returned status.
Use the sequence below. This legacy block has no completion interrupt or local abort command; GPIO recovery clears OE, and timer recovery uses root reset/selection under the board ownership policy.

mpw-gpio.title: MPW User GPIO
notes: The selected GPIO demo has independent 32-bit output-enable and output-data latches. An OE bit of one drives the corresponding user output; zero releases it. DATA_IN reads the current user-GPIO input boundary. This block does not implement pin muxing, input filtering, edge capture or interrupt state; those functions remain in the root GPIO fabric.

Write DATA_OUT before asserting the intended OE bits to avoid an unwanted initial level. Clear OE before relinquishing the user path. Reset clears both output latches. Root GPIO eligibility and the selected MPW IP still determine whether a signal reaches a physical pad.

Undefined reads return zero and undefined writes have no effect. These legacy blocks ignore PSTRB; software must use aligned full-word accesses. Neither block has a FIFO, DMA engine or dedicated interrupt.

rcu.title: Reset and Clock Unit
notes: The RCU is controlled through SYSCTRL registers; it does not own another APB address aperture. Clock roots, divisions, safe fallback and memory-pad mode remain root-management operations.
software_steps: Inspect clock status and capability; the reference profile has no enabled PLL macro.
Use rs_clock_set_frequency with a bounded timeout; traffic drain and safe-source sequencing remain controller responsibilities.
Check completion and sticky faults. Retain the safe source after a failed change.

ext-l.title: Low-Bandwidth Extension
notes: EXT-L exposes control and interrupt capability without a data master, stream interface or local SRAM. EXT-H-only data and DMA controls are not supported in this slot.
software_steps: Confirm the instance base address, active clock/reset domain and resource owner before accessing registers.
Read the identification/capability registers where present, then follow the configuration and transfer sequence above. Do not write configuration fields while an operation forbids it.
Use bounded completion checks; inspect and clear the documented event/error fields. Transfer shared-buffer ownership with the required fences and cache maintenance.
